pages.text: This is a rocket. Rockets help people and tools travel from Earth into space.
Rockets must be very strong. Earth’s gravity pulls down, so rockets push up very hard.
Inside the rocket is fuel. Fuel burns and makes hot gas that pushes the rocket upward.
When the rocket launches, it makes loud sounds and bright flames. The ground shakes a little.
Up, up, up the rocket goes, climbing higher than planes and clouds.
Space begins far above Earth. There is no air, and the sky looks very dark.
In space, things float more easily. Rockets help astronauts bring tools, food, and science to space.
Some rockets drop empty parts as they fly. This helps the rocket go farther using less fuel.
After the mission, rockets or capsules come back to Earth and land safely.
At bedtime, we remember: rockets use fuel and strength to carry people and tools into space.
